transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, uh… I guess the main thing is I just can’t seem to sit still when I’m supposed to. It’s like there’s a little motor running under my skin, if that makes sense. Like in staff meetings at work, or when I’m at church and they’re going over plans for an event, everybody else is sitting there listening, and I’m shifting around in the chair, crossing and uncrossing my legs, leaning forward, leaning back… and before long I’m standing up or finding some reason to step out or go check on something.

It’s not like I’m trying to be rude. I just get this restless feeling in my body, like I need to move, and the longer I’m expected to stay put, the worse it gets. So that’s kind of what brought me in — it’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to somebody about it.
Did this restless feeling start after you began a medication or after the dose of one was changed?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, not that I’ve noticed. I’m trying to think if there was some clear “before and after” with a pill or a dose change, but nothing like that jumps out at me.

I guess I’m not totally sure what all would count, but as far as I can tell, this restlessness doesn’t feel like it suddenly showed up right after starting something new or changing an amount. It feels more like… it’s just been part of how I am in situations where I’m expected to stay seated and still.
Did you have this same trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah… yeah, I did. I mean, looking back, that was kind of a thing even when I was little.

I remember in grade school I’d get in trouble for popping up out of my seat when we were supposed to be working quietly. The teacher would be talking, and I’d just blurt something out over her, or I’d start doing the assignment before she’d even finished giving all the directions. Not because I was trying to be a pain, at least I don’t think so — I just felt like I had to move or say the thing right then.

My mother used to say I was “wound too tight,” even as a kid. That was her phrase. Like I had too much spring in me or something. So yeah, this doesn’t feel like something that only started recently. It feels like it’s been there a long time.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, energized, or euphoric for several days in a row?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in the way you’re describing, like feeling unusually high or euphoric for days. I’ve had times where I’m busy or wound up, sure, and I can get energized if there’s a lot going on or I’m trying to get things done, but I wouldn’t say it’s like I’m on top of the world or anything like that.

I guess I’m trying to be careful how I answer, because “energized” can mean different things. I’m restless a lot, like I said, but that’s more uncomfortable than happy. I don’t remember having several days in a row where I felt unusually great or high, like way beyond my normal self.
When you feel restless in those situations, is it because you’re feeling anxious or worried?

Not really, no. I mean, I can get worried about things like anyone, but that restless feeling doesn’t usually feel like it’s coming from worry.

It’s more like… if I’m supposed to sit still, like in a staff meeting or a briefing for an event at church, I get this feeling like there’s a little motor humming under my skin. That’s the best way I can explain it. I’m sitting there trying to be polite and pay attention, but my body is just telling me to move. I’ll shift around, change how I’m sitting, stand up if I can get away with it, or find some excuse like needing to check something or grab water or straighten something up.

So it’s not usually, “Oh no, I’m scared something bad is going to happen.” It’s more just this pressure to move, like staying planted in the chair takes way more effort than it should.
